blurb: Board games, card tables and arcade cabinets across the generations

questions.q: On the classic US Monopoly board, which property costs the most to buy?
questions.fact: The classic US board's street names come from Atlantic City, New Jersey.
questions.src: wshu.org 2021-08-26 'secret behind the Monopoly board': Atlantic City names, Boardwalk $400 most expensive

questions.q: In Scrabble, how many bonus points do you earn for using all seven of your tiles in one turn?
questions.fact: Inventor Alfred Butts, an architect, first called his game Lexiko, then Criss Cross Words.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bingo_(Scrabble) (50-point bonus); en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Alfred_Mosher_Butts (architect, Lexiko, Criss Cross Words)

questions.q: Trivial Pursuit was dreamed up in 1979 by two journalists from which country?
questions.fact: Chris Haney and Scott Abbott worked out the basic idea in a few hours one December day in Montreal.
questions.src: thecanadianencyclopedia.ca/en/article/trivial-pursuit: devised 15 Dec 1979, Haney (Montreal Gazette) and Abbott (Canadian Press), concept in a few hours

questions.q: The hit board game Catan was first published in 1995 in which country?
questions.fact: Designer Klaus Teuber was working as a dental technician when he created it.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Klaus_Teuber (dental technician, 1995, Spiel des Jahres); opinionatedgamers.com SdJ re-review: published 1995 by Kosmos

questions.q: In a standard Sudoku, each row, column and box must hold which numbers?
questions.fact: The modern puzzle first ran in a 1979 Dell magazine as 'Number Place'; Japan's Nikoli later named it Sudoku.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sudoku: Garns' puzzle published 1979 by Dell as Number Place; 1890s French precursors; Nikoli (Maki Kaji) named it 1984/1986

questions.q: In Wordle, how many guesses do you get to find the hidden five-letter word?
questions.fact: Creator Josh Wardle named it as a play on his own surname; The New York Times bought it in 2022.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wordle: six attempts, NYT bought Jan 31 2022, name is a play on Wardle's surname

questions.q: The card game UNO was invented in 1971 by Merle Robbins, who worked as what?
questions.fact: He made it to settle a family argument over Crazy Eights rules, then sold the rights for $50,000 plus royalties.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Merle_Robbins: barber, Reading, Ohio; 1971; argument with son Ray over Crazy Eights; 1972 sold to International Games for $50,000 plus 10 cents/game royalties

questions.q: The earliest commercial jigsaw puzzles, sold in London in the 1760s, showed what?
questions.fact: Engraver John Spilsbury sold these 'dissected maps' as tools for teaching geography.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Spilsbury_(cartographer): engraver/cartographer, 1766, world map cut by country, 'Dissected Maps' to teach geography, 'almost certainly the earliest commercial producer' (Mme de Beaumont's 1759 wooden maps were also maps)

questions.q: Every falling piece in Tetris is made from how many squares?
questions.fact: Alexey Pajitnov created it at a Moscow computer center; the name blends 'tetra,' Greek for four, with tennis.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tetris: tetrominoes (four blocks); Pajitnov at Dorodnitsyn Computing Center, Academy of Sciences; tetra + tennis; sources differ on 1984 vs 1985, so year dropped

questions.q: In Mario Kart, the dreaded blue Spiny Shell homes in on which racer?
questions.fact: The blue shell made its debut in Mario Kart 64, first released in Japan in 1996.
questions.src: mariowiki.com/Spiny_Shell_(blue): targets the leader, first appears in Mario Kart 64; en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Blue_shell: Mario Kart 64 (1996)

questions.q: In the 1980 arcade classic Pac-Man, what is the name of the red ghost?
questions.fact: Creator Toru Iwatani has said a pizza missing a slice helped inspire Pac-Man's shape.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pac-Man: Blinky red; Iwatani pizza story, which he called only partly true (also the kanji for mouth); Japan May 1980

questions.q: Minecraft's maker, the studio Mojang, was founded in which country?
questions.fact: Microsoft bought his studio, Mojang, for $2.5 billion in 2014.
questions.src: Mojang Studios: founded 2009 in Stockholm, Sweden (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Mojang_Studios); Microsoft bought Mojang for $2.5B in 2014. Reworded Nov 2026 to leave out the creator's name.

blurb: Nicknames, the workbench and a few brain benders to start the week

questions.q: Which city is famously nicknamed 'The Big Apple'?
questions.fact: Sportswriter John J. Fitz Gerald helped popularize the name with a 1920s newspaper column.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Big_Apple: Fitz Gerald, NY Morning Telegraph sportswriter, 1920s columns, 'Around the Big Apple' Feb 18 1924

questions.q: Which nurse became known as 'The Lady with the Lamp'?
questions.fact: She earned the name making nighttime rounds of hospital wards during the Crimean War.
questions.src: Textbook history (Nightingale at Scutari, Crimean War, night rounds with a lamp)

questions.q: On The Mandalorian, the character fans nicknamed 'Baby Yoda' has what real name?
questions.fact: Ahsoka Tano reveals the name in the show's second season, which aired in 2020.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Chapter_13:_The_Jedi: Ahsoka Tano learns his name is Grogu; season 2, Disney+ Nov 27 2020

questions.q: Actor John Wayne got his famous nickname 'Duke' from what?
questions.fact: Wayne was born Marion Morrison in Winterset, Iowa, in 1907.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/John_Wayne: fireman called him 'Little Duke' after his Airedale Duke; born Marion Robert Morrison (often given as Marion Michael, so middle name dropped), Winterset, Iowa, May 26 1907

questions.q: A Phillips screwdriver has a tip shaped like what?
questions.fact: Square-drive screws are called Robertson screws, after Canadian inventor P. L. Robertson.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/P._L._Robertson: Canadian inventor; square-socket drive 'often called the Robertson drive'

questions.q: On sandpaper, what does a higher grit number such as 220 tell you?
questions.fact: Grit numbers trace back to the mesh screens once used to sort abrasive grains by size.
questions.src: seriousgrit.com 'what do the numbers mean in sandpaper': higher = finer; grains historically sorted by woven wire screens (80 mesh = 80 openings per inch), now FEPA/CAMI sieve analysis

questions.q: A standard 'two-by-four' board actually measures about how many inches?
questions.fact: It starts near 2 by 4 inches when rough-sawn, then shrinks as it is dried and planed smooth.
questions.src: hansenpolebuildings.com lumber-size: modern dry 2x4 is 1-1/2 x 3-1/2; rough-sawn was about 2 x 4; planing and drying shrink it; older planed size 1-5/8 x 3-5/8 (not an option)

questions.q: In nail sizes such as '16d,' what does the 'd' stand for?
questions.fact: The 'd' is the old British symbol for a penny, which comes from the denarius, a Roman coin.
questions.src: extremehowto.com 'why are nails designated in penny sizes' (d = penny, from denarius); worldwidewords.org qa-six2 (d = pre-decimal penny, from Latin denarius)

questions.q: A drawer holds only black and white socks. How many must you grab in the dark to be sure of a matching pair?
questions.fact: It's the pigeonhole principle: with two colors, the third sock must match one of the first two.
questions.src: Logic, solved independently: 2 can be one of each; the 3rd must match one (pigeonhole). 'Matching' added so 2 can't be argued

questions.q: Ferry a wolf, goat and cabbage over a river, one per trip. Never leave the goat with either. What goes first?
questions.fact: Versions of this river-crossing puzzle appear in a collection linked to Alcuin of York, around the year 800.
questions.src: Solved independently: wolf first leaves goat+cabbage, cabbage first leaves wolf+goat, crossing empty leaves both; only goat works. en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Wolf,_goat_and_cabbage_problem: earliest in Propositiones ad Acuendos Juvenes, linked to Alcuin, 9th c.

questions.q: A bat and ball cost $1.10 in total. The bat costs $1.00 more than the ball. How much is the ball?
questions.fact: The quick gut answer, 10 cents, is the most common wrong reply to this well-known puzzle.
questions.src: Solved: ball x, bat x+1.00, 2x+1.00=1.10, x=0.05 (10 cents gives total 1.20). Most common wrong answer 10 cents: Judgment and Decision Making 2019 (dlab.sauder.ubc.ca jdm181112) citing Frederick 2005

questions.q: What letter comes next in this series: O, T, T, F, F, S, S, ...?
questions.fact: Each letter starts a counting word: One, Two, Three, Four, Five, Six, Seven... so Eight is next.
questions.src: Solved: initials of One..Seven, next Eight. No other option fits a rule (N is Nine, after E)

blurb: Solstice week: backyard birds, maps and winter garden know-how

questions.q: Hummingbirds get their name from what?
questions.fact: Hummingbirds live only in the Americas, and the rufous hummingbird nests as far north as Alaska.
questions.src: fs.usda.gov Hummingbird Guide AK: 'Hummingbirds only occur in the Americas'; rufous hummingbirds nest in Alaska. Name from wing hum is textbook

questions.q: In the Peanuts comic strip, what is the name of Snoopy's little yellow bird friend?
questions.fact: Charles Schulz named him after the 1969 Woodstock music festival.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Woodstock_(Peanuts): first appeared 1966, named June 22 1970, named after the 1969 festival (Schulz interviews)

questions.q: In Disney's The Lion King, Zazu the royal adviser is what kind of bird?
questions.fact: Rowan Atkinson voiced Zazu in 1994, and John Oliver took the role in the 2019 remake.
questions.src: mylionking.com/wiki/Zazu: red-billed hornbill, Rowan Atkinson 1994; CBS News 'John Oliver joins Lion King reboot' (2019 remake)

questions.q: A blue jay's feathers look blue because of what?
questions.fact: Crush a blue jay feather and the blue vanishes, because the tiny structures that scatter the light are destroyed.
questions.src: bangordailynews.com 2014-01-10 'blue jays blueness is a trick of light': structural color over melanin; crushing the feather makes the blue disappear

questions.q: The phrase 'Never Eat Soggy Waffles' helps people remember what?
questions.fact: A version popular in Britain, 'Never Eat Shredded Wheat,' gives the same clockwise N-E-S-W order.
questions.src: Common mnemonic; UK school geography pages (scholeselmet.leeds.sch.uk) use 'Never Eat Shredded Wheat'

questions.q: On a topographic map, what do contour lines bunched tightly together mean?
questions.fact: On a standard USGS 1:24,000 topo map, one inch on paper equals 2,000 feet on the ground.
questions.src: Textbook map reading; 24,000 in / 12 = 2,000 ft (computed); USGS 7.5-minute quads use 1:24,000

questions.q: On the December solstice, the noon sun is directly overhead along which line?
questions.fact: That's why the December solstice brings the longest day of the year to the Southern Hemisphere.
questions.src: Textbook astronomy/geography

questions.q: Greenland looks about as big as Africa on a Mercator map. Africa is really about how many times bigger?
questions.fact: Gerardus Mercator designed the projection in 1569 to help sailors steer straight courses.
questions.src: Areas: Africa ~30.37M sq km, Greenland ~2.166M sq km, ratio 14.0 (computed); Mercator 1569 is textbook

questions.q: Trees that drop all their leaves every autumn are called what?
questions.fact: The larch is a cone-bearing tree that turns gold and drops its needles every fall.
questions.src: Textbook botany (larch is a deciduous conifer)

questions.q: The poinsettia, a popular December plant, is native to which country?
questions.fact: It's named for Joel Poinsett, the first US minister to Mexico, who sent it north in the 1820s.
questions.src: nbcnewyork.com poinsettia history: native to Mexico (Pacific coast, into Central America); Joel Poinsett, first US minister to Mexico, found it 1828 and sent clippings home to South Carolina

questions.q: On holly, which plants grow the bright red berries?
questions.fact: Most hollies need a male plant nearby so its pollen can reach the berry-bearing females.
questions.src: gardeningknowhow.com male vs female holly: 'all females produce berries. Males do not'; a male must be close by (Chinese holly can berry without one, still female)

questions.q: USDA plant hardiness zones are based on what?
questions.fact: Each zone spans 10 degrees Fahrenheit and is split into 'a' and 'b' halves of 5 degrees.
questions.src: extension.purdue.edu 2023 USDA map story: average annual extreme minimum winter temperature; 13 zones of 10 F; a/b half zones of 5 F

blurb: A cozy, easy mix by the fire: home comforts, famous pairs and letters

questions.q: What do you call the shelf above a fireplace?
questions.fact: The hearth is the fireproof floor of the fireplace, often reaching out into the room.
questions.src: Textbook household vocabulary

questions.q: A classic quilt is made of how many layers?
questions.fact: The soft middle layer, tucked between the top and the backing, is called batting.
questions.src: Textbook quilting (top, batting, backing)

questions.q: On a laundry care tag, what does a square with a circle inside mean?
questions.fact: A plain circle means dry clean, and a triangle covers bleach instructions.
questions.src: expertreviews.co.uk laundry symbols: circle in square = tumble dry; plain circle = dry cleaning; triangle = bleach

questions.q: What is the metal flap that closes off a chimney when the fire is out?
questions.fact: Andirons are the metal stands that lift logs so air can flow underneath them.
questions.src: Textbook fireplace vocabulary

questions.q: In the comic strip Calvin and Hobbes, Hobbes is a stuffed what?
questions.fact: Bill Watterson named the pair after theologian John Calvin and philosopher Thomas Hobbes.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bill_Watterson: in The Complete Calvin and Hobbes he names the 16th-century theologian and 17th-century philosopher

questions.q: Sonic the Hedgehog's two-tailed sidekick, Tails, is what kind of animal?
questions.fact: His full name is Miles 'Tails' Prower, a pun on 'miles per hour.'
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tails_(Sonic_the_Hedgehog): fox; 'Miles Prower is a pun on miles per hour'

questions.q: In the classic cartoon, Rocky the flying squirrel's best pal Bullwinkle is what animal?
questions.fact: The pair hailed from the fictional town of Frostbite Falls, Minnesota.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Bullwinkle_J._Moose: moose; Frostbite Falls, Minnesota (spoof of International Falls)

questions.q: Which comedy duo made the baseball routine 'Who's on First?' famous?
questions.fact: Bud Abbott played the straight man to Lou Costello, and they performed the bit for years on radio and film.
questions.src: baseballhall.org 'Who's on First': Abbott the straight man; Kate Smith Hour radio 1938; film The Naughty Nineties 1945

questions.q: 'The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog' is famous for containing what?
questions.fact: A sentence that uses every letter is called a pangram, and typists have practiced on this one for generations.
questions.src: Checked with python: contains all 26 letters; has repeats; 'over' and 'lazy' are two syllables; 9 words

questions.q: Which letter is used most often in written English?
questions.fact: In Morse code, E gets the shortest signal of all: a single dot.
questions.src: Letter frequency textbook; cs4fn.org Alfred Vail: E is a single dot as the most common letter (code letters largely Vail's work, so Morse credit dropped)

questions.q: On a standard phone keypad, which number key also carries the letters P, Q, R and S?
questions.fact: On many older US phones, the 7 key showed only P, R and S, with no Q.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Telephone_keypad: modern 7 = PQRS, 9 = WXYZ; older phones had 7 = PRS, 9 = WXY ('classic' changed to 'standard')

questions.q: Which letter of the alphabet appears in none of the 50 US state names?
questions.fact: J appears in just one state name, New Jersey, and Z only in Arizona.
questions.src: Checked with python over all 50 state names: q absent; j only New Jersey; z only Arizona; x in Texas and New Mexico

blurb: Trains and planes, decade guessing and America's national parks

questions.q: In Harry Potter, the Hogwarts Express leaves London from which platform?
questions.fact: London's King's Cross station has a 'Platform 9 3/4' sign with a luggage cart half-vanished into the wall.
questions.src: Books/films textbook; atlasobscura.com/places/platform-9-3-4: marker with a baggage trolley disappearing into the wall at King's Cross

questions.q: Which Boeing airliner earned the nickname 'Jumbo Jet'?
questions.fact: Its famous hump holds the cockpit and an upper deck, which early airlines used as a lounge.
questions.src: insideflyer.com '747 upper deck evolved from lounge to cargo asset': cockpit above main deck; original -100s used the upper deck as lounges

questions.q: On a plane or a ship, which side is called 'port'?
questions.fact: Planes carry a red light on the left wingtip and a green one on the right, just like ships.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Navigation_light: red on left wingtip, green on right, following marine convention (red port)

questions.q: Howard Hughes' giant 'Spruce Goose' flying boat was built mostly from what wood?
questions.fact: It flew only once, in 1947, for about a mile at roughly 70 feet above the water.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Hughes_H-4_Hercules: 'made almost entirely of birch' (Duramold); only flight Nov 2 1947, about 1 mile, about 70 ft up, 26 seconds

questions.q: Disneyland first opened its gates in California in which decade?
questions.fact: Walt Disney World in Florida followed in 1971.
questions.src: AP 'This Day in History July 17' (wtap.com 2026-07-17): Disneyland opened July 17 1955 (construction began 1954); Walt Disney World opened Oct 1 1971

questions.q: The first US transcontinental railroad was completed in which decade?
questions.fact: A ceremonial golden spike marked its completion at Promontory Summit, Utah.
questions.src: Textbook US history: golden spike, Promontory Summit, May 10 1869; construction 1863-69, all inside the 1860s

questions.q: AT&T's toll-free '800' phone numbers were first introduced in which decade?
questions.fact: Toll-free numbers that spell words with keypad letters are called phonewords; they boomed in the 1980s and 1990s.
questions.src: en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Phoneword: 'Toll-free numbering, as originally introduced by AT&T in 1967'; phonewords grew in the 1980s and 1990s

questions.q: The US 'Forever' stamp, good for first-class mail even after prices rise, debuted in which decade?
questions.fact: The first Forever stamp, issued in April 2007, pictured the Liberty Bell.
questions.src: news.usps.com 2024-04-12 'One for the ages': first Forever stamp, the Liberty Bell, issued April 12 2007

questions.q: Cartoon character Yogi Bear's 'Jellystone Park' is a spoof of which national park?
questions.fact: Yogi Bear debuted in 1958 on The Huckleberry Hound Show and got his own series in 1961.
questions.src: centerofthewest.org 2017-01-07 'Yellowstone, Jellystone, Yogi Bear': Jellystone inspired by Yellowstone; Yogi debuted Oct 1958 on The Huckleberry Hound Show, own show 1961

questions.q: Which animal appears on the National Park Service's arrowhead emblem?
questions.fact: The emblem also shows a sequoia tree, mountains and water; the arrowhead shape stands for history.
questions.src: nps.gov/mana 'The National Park Service Arrowhead': sequoia and bison (plants, wildlife), mountains and water (scenery, recreation), arrowhead (historical and archeological values)

questions.q: The giant tree named General Sherman grows in which national park?
questions.fact: It's a giant sequoia, and its trunk measures more than 100 feet around at the ground.
questions.src: nps.gov/seki/learn/nature/sherman.htm: north end of Giant Forest (Sequoia NP); circumference at ground 102.6 ft. Kings Canyon dropped (NPS runs them as one unit)

questions.q: Theodore Roosevelt National Park is in which state?
questions.fact: Roosevelt ran cattle ranches in the Dakota Badlands in the 1880s, before he became president.
questions.src: home.nps.gov/thro 'Theodore Roosevelt the Rancher': entered ranching 1883, Maltese Cross and Elkhorn ranches near Medora; park address Medora, ND
